topic: How do distributed satellite constellations impact orbital configuration trade-offs between coverage and inter-satellite interference mitigation?
consensus_response: Distributed satellite constellations introduce complexity in mission design, antenna array management, and frequency allocation, impacting orbital configuration trade-offs. Increased satellites lead to increased interference, reducing capacity. Higher orbit altitudes decrease signal strength, reducing coverage. Orbital diversity can mitigate interference by allocating orthogonal wireless resources, but requires careful consideration of mission requirements and operational constraints. Frequency reuse can also reduce interference while maintaining high capacity, but strict synchronization is required for scalable networks.
reference_context: Distributed satellite constellations have been widely investigated for connectivity aspects, with some studies focusing on inter-plane inter-satellite communication to fully unleash the potential of LEO satellite constellations and facilitate their integration with 5G.
